title: VF-MT307-ReconcilerPropertyTests
clause: proptest-state-machine over step() against a reference model with convergence and never-two-live-VMs invariants; trait-mocked CH adapter harness with named crash-injection regressions including spawn-succeeds-then-process-dies; deterministic seeds; no madsim product dependency

scope.summary:
GOAL: Prove the fleet reconciler's core logic correct under adversarial interleavings, crashes, and stale generations - the verification layer the research basis says the pure-step() design exists to enable (P21: 'the pure-step() design in P20 is what makes the cheap option (proptest over the pure function + a fake CH adapter + fake clock) sufficient without swapping runtimes'). Two deliverables: (A) a proptest-state-machine suite that drives MT-303's pure step() against an abstract reference model, and (B) a deterministic integration harness over a trait-mocked CH adapter with NAMED crash-injection regression cases. Explicitly NO madsim (or any simulation-runtime crate) as a product dependency - the research avoid-clause warns against forcing runtime abstraction through the whole product; determinism comes from planner purity, pre-drawn jitter (MT-304 design), injected clocks, and recorded proptest seeds.

(A) PROPTEST-STATE-MACHINE SUITE (research P21, docs.rs/proptest-state-machine):
   Reference model: a small abstract fleet - for each worktree: abstract desired (Running/Snapshotted/Absent), abstract observed (subset: NoVm, VmStarting, VmAliveHealthy, VmAliveNoHeartbeat, VmDeadProcess, Paused, Quarantined, Tombstoned, ArchivedGone), plus desired_generation and binding_generation counters.
   Transitions (proptest-generated command sequences): SetDesired(state), VmDies, HeartbeatArrives, HeartbeatGoesStale, CrashReconcilerMidPlan(step_index), StaleGenerationWrite, RequestTeardown, QuarantineEnter, QuarantineClear, RunOnePass (applies step() to current observed/desired and executes the plan against the model).
   INVARIANTS (checked after every command):
   INV-1 CONVERGENCE: from any reachable state, executing converged passes (RunOnePass repeated with no new perturbations) reaches a state where observed matches desired within a bounded number of passes ('one more converged pass reaches desired state' generalized: bound asserted, default <= 3 passes absent failures) - per P21's stated property 'after any sequence of crashes/restarts/stale generations, one more converged pass reaches desired state'.
   INV-2 SINGLE-VM: at no point do two live VMs exist for one worktree ('never double-spawns a VM for one worktree') - the model counts spawns minus verified kills per worktree and asserts <= 1 live.
   INV-3 FENCING: a StaleGenerationWrite command never mutates model state (writes with generation < current are rejected), mirroring MT-303 AC-303-6.
   INV-4 NO-LOSS: a Tombstoned worktree never transitions to ArchivedGone while any cleanup obligation (live VM, unreleased lease, unarchived manifest) remains - MT-305's ordering invariant.
   INV-5 QUARANTINE-STICKY: Quarantined never exits via RunOnePass alone; only QuarantineClear (or the MT-304 full-success rule, modeled explicitly) exits.
   Shrinking + seeds: failures must shrink to a minimal transition sequence; the proptest RNG seed configuration is committed so any failure is replayable byte-for-byte (deterministic seeds requirement); failure regressions get persisted via proptest's regression-file mechanism checked into the test tree.

(B) TRAIT-MOCKED ADAPTER HARNESS (research P21, P10/flintlock #326): a MockSandboxAdapter implementing the SandboxAdapter trait (the same trait CloudHypervisorAdapter implements - spawn line 2000, kill 2314, status 2398, snapshot 2444, restore 2649 in adapter.rs; the fake-adapter precedent already exists in the WP-1 test tree per worktree_vm_registry.rs module doc 'fake-adapter-tested seam', line 15) with scriptable failure injection: per-call-site programmable outcomes (Ok, Err, Ok-then-process-vanishes, hang-until-cancelled), a step-recording journal for assertion, and an injected clock for heartbeat freshness.
   NAMED REGRESSION CASES (each a #[test] with the research citation in a comment):
   REG-1 spawn_succeeds_then_process_dies: spawn returns Ok, status flips to non-Running before first heartbeat -> planner must hold Pending, then plan cleanup + respawn; VM never reported Running (flintlock #326, P10).
   REG-2 crash_between_pause_and_snapshot: PausedForSnapshot crash point -> next pass completes capture + resume without data loss (P13).
   REG-3 crash_between_snapshot_and_resume: snapshot captured, resume lost -> next pass resumes; no second snapshot taken (P13, idempotence P2).
   REG-4 stale_generation_racing_writer: two planned passes, first commits, second (stale fence) writes zero rows and errors typed (P14 fencing; worktree_vm_registry.rs StaleBinding discipline 1104-1162).
   REG-5 teardown_of_never_created_vm: tombstone on a workspace with no VM -> archived cleanly (P4; MT-305 AC-305-4).
   REG-6 restore_hang_cancelled_by_shutdown: restore hangs, shutdown requested -> in-flight step drains per MT-302 semantics, journal shows intent record and no post-cancel side effect (P18/P19).
   REG-7 double_dispatch_race: two concurrent claims for one worktree -> the conditional SurrealDB claim-lease transaction admits one; the other observes claim-miss; exactly one spawn recorded (INV-2 at the integration layer).
   Harness rules: mock adapter and injected clock live in test code only (dev-dependencies / #[cfg(test)]); zero product-code changes except where a seam is genuinely missing, in which case the seam addition is the minimal injection point (constructor parameter, not a cfg-gated fork) and is called out in the completion report.

RESOURCE PRIVACY: property and integration tests instantiate scoped contexts (two distinct account scopes in at least one property run) and assert the reference model never observes cross-scope effects, consistent with the resource_scope patterns (resource_scope.rs ResourceScope 147-153); this keeps the privacy invariant under test, not just under code review.

SPEC-REALISM NOTE: the property suite is deliberately pure (that is its power); realism is preserved because (1) the integration harness's fencing/journaling regressions (REG-4 especially) run against REAL SurrealDB with the mock only at the adapter boundary, and (2) MT-301..305 each carry their own live-SurrealDB proofs. Fixture-only proof of the WHOLE family is thereby avoided: this MT's live-SurrealDB surface is the fencing/journaling/claim behavior, which is exactly the part SurrealDB owns.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: new test files under src/backend/handshake_core/tests/ (e.g. vm_fleet_property_tests.rs, vm_fleet_regression_tests.rs) plus a tests-support module for the mock adapter, reference model, and injected clock; proptest + proptest-state-machine added as dev-dependencies in Cargo.toml (dev-dependencies only - grep-enforced); proptest regression files checked in.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read MT-303's landed lifecycle.rs/executor.rs, MT-302's dispatcher claim path, the SandboxAdapter trait, and the existing fake-adapter test utilities in the WP-1 test tree (reuse before building - the registry's fake-adapter seam is the starting point).
2. Build the reference model + transition strategy; wire proptest-state-machine with committed seed configuration.
3. Implement INV-1..INV-5 checks; run until stable; commit any shrunk regressions.
4. Build MockSandboxAdapter + injected clock; implement REG-1..REG-7 with research citations in comments.
5. Wire REG-4 (and the claim race REG-7) against real SurrealDB.
6. Run the full suite twice with the same seeds and diff outputs to prove determinism; record measured output.
7. Implementer never marks COMPLETED.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/vm_fleet/** (minimal injection seams only, called out in report)
forbidden_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/sandbox/** (mock implements the trait; the real adapter is untouched)
acceptance_criteria: AC-307-1: A proptest-state-machine suite drives step() against an abstract reference model through generated command sequences including crashes, restarts, stale generations, teardowns, and quarantine events.
AC-307-2: INV-1 convergence holds: after any generated perturbation sequence, bounded converged passes (default <= 3) reach desired state - the P21 property stated verbatim in a test comment.
AC-307-3: INV-2 holds: the model never observes two live VMs for one worktree across any generated sequence.
AC-307-4: INV-3/INV-4/INV-5 (stale-fence rejection, no-archive-with-obligations, quarantine stickiness) are checked after every command and hold.

AC-307-5: Failures shrink to minimal sequences and replay deterministically from committed seed configuration; proptest regression files are checked in; the full suite run twice with identical seeds produces identical results (determinism proof target).

AC-307-6: MockSandboxAdapter implements the SandboxAdapter trait with programmable per-call outcomes including Ok-then-process-vanishes and hang-until-cancelled, plus a call journal and injected clock - test-code only (dev-dependency/#[cfg(test)]), grep-proof no mock in product code paths.

AC-307-7: Named regressions REG-1..REG-7 exist and pass, each with its research citation in a comment; REG-1 is the flintlock #326 spawn-succeeds-then-process-dies case and asserts the VM is never reported Running.
AC-307-8: REG-4 and REG-7 run against real SurrealDB, proving stale fencing writes affect zero records and a conditional claim-lease race admits exactly one current claimant.
AC-307-9: No madsim, no simulation-runtime crate, and no K8s/Docker/containerd/Nomad/SQLite identifiers anywhere (grep proof over Cargo.toml including dev-dependencies for madsim specifically).

AC-307-10: Any product-code injection seam added is minimal (constructor parameter), justified in the completion report, and leaves production behavior unchanged (proven by the existing MT-301..305 test suites still passing).

implementation_notes: IMPLEMENTATION GATE: gated on WP-1 IV verdicts + merge to main (expansion_provenance.implementation_gate); MT-303 must land first. MT-304/305 semantics (quarantine stickiness, finalizer ordering) are modeled abstractly if those MTs have not merged yet, with the model updated when they land - note which version was modeled in the completion report.

No madsim is a hard rule from the research avoid-clause: 'adopting madsim wholesale... forces runtime abstraction through the whole product; only the reconciler crate needs determinism' - and planner purity makes even that unnecessary.
Reuse the existing WP-1 fake-adapter utilities before writing a new mock; extend rather than duplicate (GLOBAL-RESEARCH-039 reuse discipline).

The convergence bound (<= 3 passes) is a contract default; if a legitimate plan legitimately needs more passes (e.g. teardown chains), raise the bound with a comment justifying the exact worst case, never remove the bound.
All Rust; SurrealDB for the live-fencing regressions; no SQLite; disk-agnostic paths; no names with spaces; per-owner CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ../Handshake_Artifacts/.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Test-suite MT; its output surface is test results and checked-in regression files. GUI verification for the fleet lives in MT-306.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Test-only MT; no runtime behavior change to record. FR coverage of the tested paths is MT-306's.
Test-only MT; diagnostic surfaces of the product paths are owned by MT-303/304/305.
No long-lived process is introduced; the harness runs inside cargo test.

risk_if_missed: The reconciler's correctness rests entirely on example-based tests: interleaving bugs (double spawn under claim races, lost paused snapshots, stale-fence bypasses) ship undetected, and the flintlock #326 class of failure - the single most-cited field bug in the research basis - has no named regression guarding against reintroduction.

risks: RISK-1: The reference model unconsciously mirrors the implementation's bugs (same author, same assumptions), making properties vacuously green.
RISK-2: Mock adapter or injected clock leaks into product code paths, changing production behavior under test flags.
RISK-3: Non-deterministic test ordering or unseeded RNG makes failures unreproducible, destroying the suite's diagnostic value.
RISK-4: The convergence bound is quietly raised or removed when a bug makes convergence slow, converting a correctness property into a no-op.
RISK-5: madsim or another simulation runtime creeps in as a transitive product dependency.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): The model is abstract (state sets, counters) rather than a re-implementation of step(); invariants INV-1..5 are stated from the research properties, not from code behavior; WP validator reviews model-vs-code independence.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Mock lives in test code only; grep proof AC-307-6 + MT-301..305 suites still passing AC-307-10.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Committed seed configuration + two-run diff proof target (AC-307-5).
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Bound changes require an in-code justification comment naming the exact worst case; validator checks the diff for silent bound edits.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Cargo.toml grep proof including dev-dependencies (AC-307-9).

surrealdb_translation_v02_205.schema_rule: Any embedded PostgreSQL DDL/SQL snippet is a semantic field/index/invariant inventory only. Implement it as SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL through SurrealKit; do not execute or mechanically transliterate the snippet.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.concurrency_rule: Translate advisory locks, SKIP LOCKED and row locks into SurrealDB transactions, durable lease/fencing records and conditional updates with equivalent tests.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.notification_rule: Translate LISTEN/NOTIFY into scoped SurrealDB live queries plus bounded resynchronization.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.privacy_rule: Translate RLS into authenticated record-user table/field PERMISSIONS intersected with ResourceBroker; administrative credentials cannot prove privacy.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.proof_rule: All named storage proofs run against real SurrealDB. No PostgreSQL process, driver, connection, fixture, environment variable or fallback is permitted.
